subject: series
synopsis: A licensed comic adaptation of the cult horror film franchise, featuring the ancient demonic Creeper in new hunting stories that expand on the creature's terrifying mythology beyond the films.

synopsis: Character-focused Infinity Comics

synopsis: The origin arc of Jennifer Blood, the suburban housewife who moonlights as a brutal vigilante assassin, by Garth Ennis.

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar and John McCrea's five-issue tour through the century-long life of Jenny Sparks, the Authority's leader and spirit of the 20th century.

subject: series
synopsis: An early BOOM Studios sci-fi action miniseries featuring a hard-boiled interplanetary bounty hunter. Standard genre fare that showed BOOM's early ambitions as a sci-fi comics publisher.
author: Keith Giffen

subject: series
synopsis: A Europe Comics series with introspective character study and emotional depth.

subject: series
synopsis: An anthology of witch folktales from around the world in the spirit of Jim Henson's The Storyteller, each adapted by a different cartoonist.

subject: series
synopsis: A manga by Touya Tobina about a young female huntress who raises two werewolf twins who are devoted to her. A supernatural romance/comedy with a dark premise given a relatively lighthearted treatment.
author: Touya Tobina

subject: series
synopsis: Omnibus collecting Mike Mignola and Christopher Golden's noir-supernatural series about a detective in a flooded, steampunk-esque Lower Manhattan, set in the 1970s.
author: Mike Mignola

subject: series
synopsis: Sam Humphries' adaptation of Edgar Rice Burroughs' second Barsoom novel following John Carter's return to Mars.
author: Sam Humphries

subject: series
synopsis: A sci-fi western about a small town in the future American frontier caught between a megacorporation offering technological salvation and the communities that reject it. author: Matt Kindt

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Horror crossover event pitting the werewolf Jughead against Vampironica in a monster battle for Riverdale's soul.
author: Frank Tieri

subject: series
synopsis: David Lapham's all-ages adventure following a secret team of kids who battle giant underground insects threatening their small California town, blending Lapham's crime instincts with a surprisingly effective all-ages adventure that doesn't talk down to young readers.
author: David Lapham

subject: series
synopsis: Mark Millar and Frank Quitely's epic about aging Golden Age superheroes and the children who can't live up to their legacy. Quitely's art is extraordinary; Millar's generational drama is compelling even when the politics get muddy.
author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: Bob Schreck's IDW sequel to Jurassic Park focuses on the Hammond family dealing with a new dinosaur outbreak, offering franchise continuity for fans of the films rather than original drama.
author: Bob Schreck

subject: series
synopsis: R.L. Stine's BOOM! horror anthology series for younger readers, translating the Goosebumps-creator's sensibility to a connected comics universe of spooky stories. Competent all-ages horror with Stine's trademark approachable scariness.
author: R.L. Stine

subject: series
synopsis: James Robinson's controversial 7-issue miniseries launched a splinter JLA team pursuing proactive justice and ended with a shocking character death that divided readers sharply. The morally retrograde characterization of established heroes and the abrupt tragedy make this one of the more criticized events of its era.
author: James Robinson

subject: series
synopsis: A Lion Forge Catalyst Prime series about a mysterious armored hero whose abilities are fueled by his emotional state, set against the geopolitical backdrop of the shared Catalyst Prime universe.

subject: series
synopsis: Zac Thompson and Germán García's five-issue mini in which Ka-Zar, Shanna and their family face a threat to the Savage Land's ecosystem.

subject: series
synopsis: Kazu Kibuishi's celebrated anthology series featuring stunning all-ages short comics from a rotating lineup of talented cartoonists, each volume showcasing beautiful character-driven stories in a wide range of styles. A landmark anthology that launched many careers.
author: Kazu Kibuishi

subject: series
synopsis: Series spotlighting Kevin Keller, Archie Comics' first gay character, in all-ages stories about friendship, identity, and life in Riverdale.
author: Dan Parent

subject: series
synopsis: Dark Horse's Norse-mythology action series follows a family bound to the Viking age forever, forced to battle their way through a world that refuses to let them die.
author: Matt Kindt

subject: series
synopsis: Conor McCreery and Anthony Del Col's ambitious mashup pits Hamlet, Falstaff, Juliet, and Othello against a Shakespeare-villain alliance led by Richard III and Iago, building a surprisingly earnest adventure from the bones of the Western canon.
author: Conor McCreery

subject: series
synopsis: Ed Brubaker and Sean Phillips' morality thriller about a young man who believes a demon has saved his life in exchange for him killing one evil person per month. Phillips' street-level New York art is perfect; the book raises genuinely interesting questions about vigilante justice.
author: Ed Brubaker

subject: series
synopsis: A crime thriller set in the music industry, following a detective investigating murders connected to a legendary rock band. Blends noir detective fiction with music world atmosphere.
author: Ollie Masters

subject: series
synopsis: A continuation of Magdalene Visaggio's queer bounty-hunter road-trip series Kim & Kim, maintaining the series' signature blend of trans visibility, anarchic humor, and genuine emotional warmth in a vibrant sci-fi setting.
author: Magdalene Visaggio

subject: series
synopsis: A Deadpool series in which Wade Wilson becomes the King of the Monsters on Staten Island, ruling over Marvel's most dangerous creatures while still managing to make everything as chaotic as possible.
author: Kelly Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: A CrossGen action-adventure series blending espionage and humor.

subject: series
synopsis: Victor Gischler and Juan Ferreyra's New Orleans supernatural noir following a fallen angel protecting a witch from werewolf assassins hired by a demon crime lord, blending hardboiled genre elements with Catholic mythology and lush, painterly artwork.

subject: series
synopsis: DC's 2023 horror event traps heroes in nightmare realms created by Insomnia.
author: Joshua Williamson

subject: series
synopsis: A time-traveling knight is unstuck in time and must navigate different historical eras while pursuing an ancient enemy. Agustin Padilla's series blends medieval fantasy with time-travel adventure.

synopsis: Action fantasy pitting medieval knights against feudal samurai in an alternate-history clash.
author: Various

subject: series

author: Ales Kot

subject: series
synopsis: Nathan Fairbairn and Matt Smith's unique medieval horror drops an alien invasion into 13th-century Crusader France — a collision of historical faith and cold science-fiction terror rendered with gorgeous period atmosphere.
author: Nathan Fairbairn

subject: series
synopsis: A fantasy horror series from Aftershock about ancient gods and the mortals who must navigate their dangerous world. Mythology-adjacent horror with action elements.

subject: series
synopsis: A Boom Studios fantasy series about order, law, and moral codes in a complex world.

subject: series
synopsis: A two-issue prestige format limited series by Chuck Dixon and Eduardo Barreto presenting the Justice League in a medieval fantasy alternate world as knights and wizards rather than superheroes.
author: Chuck Dixon

subject: series
synopsis: John O'Bryan's story adapting the League of Legends character Lux in a fantasy kingdom torn between an oppressive mage order and a rebellious underground.
author: John O'Bryan

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Comics based on Disney's beloved film and animated series following the Hawaiian girl Lilo and her alien 'dog' Stitch in Kauai.
author: Various

subject: series
synopsis: Mindy Newell and Gray Morrow's 1986 two-issue prestige mini in which Lois Lane investigates a child-abduction ring.

subject: series
synopsis: A spinoff of the classic Lone Wolf and Cub in a futuristic setting — Lone Wolf 2100 — reimagining the ronin-and-child premise in a cyberpunk future. A creative genre mashup though it lacks the gravitas of the original.
author: Mike Kennedy

subject: series

author: Zac Thompson

subject: series
synopsis: Christopher Hastings' irreverent mini-series in which the luck-powered Longshot accidentally becomes the center of a cosmic threat to reality.
author: Christopher Hastings

subject: series
synopsis: Obscure series with incomplete run. Death's Head connection but limited standalone recognition.

subject: series
synopsis: An early IDW horror/supernatural series.

subject: series
synopsis: Zack Kaplan and Alvaro Sarraseca's YA adventure about teenagers who discover a hidden city beneath New York City and the dangerous secret their parents were protecting.
author: Zack Kaplan

subject: series
synopsis: Ales Kot and Luca Casalanguida's Vietnam War story following American and North Vietnamese soldiers who are captured and held together in surreal conditions, exploring trauma, humanity, and the psychological cost of war with quiet intensity and emotional honesty.
author: Ales Kot

subject: series
synopsis: Omnibus edition of Ken Akamatsu's classic harem romantic comedy following Keitaro Urashima as he becomes the manager of an all-girls dormitory while studying to enter Tokyo University to fulfill a childhood promise.
author: Ken Akamatsu

subject: series
synopsis: Andrew Wheeler's queer teen rom-com: Domo is torn between two potential boyfriends while competing for the captaincy of his school's tug-of-war team.

subject: series

A gentle, understated romance distinguished by its quiet charm and the contrast between the characters' inner lives and outer appearances.
author: Fuka Mizutani

subject: series
synopsis: Cinebook's collected editions of Morris and Goscinny's Lucky Luke, the cowboy who shoots faster than his shadow, roaming the Wild West against the Dalton brothers.

subject: series
synopsis: A Luke Cage tie-in to the Gang War event exploring street-level heroism amid crime conflicts.

author: Run (Guillaume Renard)

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Garth Ennis and Carlos Ezquerra's Boys spinoff following Kev Hawkins — the SAS soldier who regularly crossed paths with the Authority — in his own deadpan violent misadventures.

synopsis: Elliott Kalan and Andrea Mutti's horror-satire about a city that has learned to live with a machete-wielding killer who has haunted New York for decades, following the detective tasked with finally stopping him.

author: Kim Hyung-min

subject: series
synopsis: A CrossGen limited series tied into the larger Negation/Sigilverse mythology, focusing on the villainous Charon whose machinations drive much of CrossGen's cosmic storyline.

author: Wataru Yoshizumi

subject: series
synopsis: Archival collections reprinting the classic Mars Attacks trading card art and original stories in comics form.

subject: series
synopsis: Seasonal anthology stories

subject: series
synopsis: Brahm Revel's story following Wolverine, Kitty Pryde, and Rogue investigating the disappearance of mutant teenagers in rural Appalachia.
author: Brahm Revel

author: Frank Marraffino

synopsis: He-Man and friends face a new universe-threatening crisis in this continuation of the Netflix animated series.

synopsis: Action sci-fi with mechs and monsters

subject: series

subject: series
synopsis: Zack Kaplan and Jee-Hyung Lee's sci-fi action series set in a world where robots have replaced human athletes and the sports arena has become the venue for robot gladiatorial combat — until one robot begins questioning its purpose. Smart premise.

subject: series
synopsis: Michael Avon Oeming's (Powers co-creator) dark superhero series following a team of heroes in a near-future city ravaged by a drug called Meth — exploring trauma, addiction, and the psychological cost of wearing a mask.

subject: series
synopsis: AfterShock's series variant on the journey/odyssey narrative.

author: Mark Millar

subject: series
synopsis: Jim McCann and Rodin Esquejo's supernatural mystery following a young woman in a coma whose consciousness is trapped between worlds, desperately trying to communicate with the living to unravel who attacked her. Densely plotted mystery thriller with gorgeous covers.

subject: series
synopsis: The official Minecraft tie-in comic series following new players exploring and surviving the blocky world.

synopsis: Paul Allor and Chris Evenhuis's steampunk adventure featuring Leonardo da Vinci and a mechanical automaton during the Renaissance.
author: Paul Allor

subject: series
synopsis: Alejandro Jodorowsky and François Boucq's surreal fable: a mute, moon-faced wanderer arrives on a tyrannized island and sparks a spiritual revolution.

subject: series
synopsis: Quirky early 1990s series with dark humor. Cult status but limited mainstream recognition.

subject: series
synopsis: A Boom Studios character-driven drama series.

subject: series
synopsis: Ted Anderson and Jen Hickman's cyberpunk caper about the child of two legendary thieves who assumes their identities to infiltrate an underground crime network while searching for their missing parents.

subject: series

subject: series

synopsis: A My Little Pony miniseries set at a summer camp with adventure and friendship themes for younger readers.

subject: series
synopsis: A My Little Pony miniseries following pony characters on a nautical adventure on the high seas.

subject: series
synopsis: A landmark early manga by Kazuo Umezu (published as 'The Perfect Edition' by Viz), about two elementary school friends, Sato and Marin, who become fascinated by SHINGO, a lonely industrial robot they befriend. As Shingo develops feelings and awareness, the story explores themes of loneliness, the nature of consciousness, and what it means to be alive. One of Umezu's finest works, mixing warmth with existential dread.

subject: series
synopsis: A Sherlock Holmes spin-off following Mycroft Holmes - Sherlock's smarter, lazier brother - investigating a world-threatening conspiracy. Smart Victorian adventure.

author: Hiroyuki Takei

subject: series
synopsis: A new arc in Mark Millar's Nemesis franchise following the world's most dangerous supervillain, expanding on the high-octane thriller premise of the original series with new antagonists and escalating set pieces.

synopsis: Variant cover gallery for the 2024 Nightwing series.

synopsis: OMAC, the One Man Army Corps, fights for the common man in a corporate dystopia.

subject: series

synopsis: Marcus Parks and Henry Zebrowski of The Last Podcast on the Left, with David Rubín, on a covert team of vampire hunters in a gonzo horror-comedy.

synopsis: Marc Sumerak's mini-series depicting Storm's youth in Cairo as a young thief learning to harness her weather powers.

synopsis: Variant cover gallery for the 2024 Power Girl series.

synopsis: Ryan North's charming all-ages story of the Power Pack kids balancing school life with superheroics.
author: Ryan North
